model_answer: I would label a golden set with humans I trust, run the grader on the same cases, and count the agreement rate. I would report the false passes and the false fails apart, not one number, because they cost different things. In CI I would block a change only when the new interval sits fully below the old one's.
prompt: How do you calibrate a model grader, and what do you report?
rubric: Labels a golden set with humans before trusting the grader
Reports the agreement rate and counts the false passes and false fails apart
Says which way the grader errs matters more than one agreement number
Blocks in CI only when the new interval sits fully below the old one's

model_answer: Contamination is a test case the model saw while it learned or while I tuned, so the score measures memory. I keep a held-out set I never tune on. To catch a grader that passes for the wrong reason, I read each passing transcript next to the file: a reply that says done while the check fails is the sign.
